findings.reason: the plan must state that the shared owner preserves the validation-error raise (or the single-state entry point does), or the node will either break the malformed-answer contract or redden the cited test with no guidance on which behaviour is intended.
findings.text: §2 says _call_judgment "re-implements the fail-soft handling" and directs that deleted callers be routed through decide_batch, but _call_judgment's handling is not the same fail-soft: imas_codex/ids/candidates.py:352 re-raises DecisionsValidationError and returns None only for other transport faults, while decide_batch (imas_codex/discovery/base/judgment.py:119-124) catches "Exception" wholesale and reports None; a sync entry point built on decide_batch therefore inherits the swallow, so a malformed answer becomes a silent unjudged state, and tests/ids/test_candidate_judgment.py:124 (test_malformed_answer_is_rejected) drives judge_candidates and asserts the error propagates — so the stated mechanism cannot satisfy §2's own done-when ("tests/ids and tests/discovery suites add no failures against their base") without an unstated change to the shared owner

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: pass — verified against the tree: decide_batch at imas_codex/discovery/base/judgment.py:69, _call_judgment at imas_codex/ids/candidates.py:331, discrimination_metrics and verdict_flip_quality in imas_codex/standard_names/benchmark_roles.py (:1201, :205), the Spearman agreement in benchmark.py, test_category_gate_reproduces_source_label_auc in tests/discovery/test_path_category_gate.py:122, and the fixture labelled-path-categories.json; the control's interval 0.8858–0.9608 is documented as a 1,000-resample canonical-unit bootstrap in path-category-gate.html, so §3's done-when matches the recorded method.
rubric_items.done_when: pass — both changed sections name a control that can fail: §2 "removing the shared owner's cost-booking line turns the candidate spend assertion red" beside the delta-against-base suite check, and §3 "each test fails when its function is reverted to a stub" beside the category-gate positive control.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — §4's fixtures live under docs/evidence/fragments/sn-judgment-evaluation/ and §3's control reads docs/evidence/fragments/discovery-judgments-through-jev/, both durable; neither changed unit routes evidence through a scratchpad or node-local temporary.
rubric_items.naming: pass — the new symbols (load_labelled_fixture, paired_auc, bootstrap_interval, classification_metrics, choose_operating_point, frozen_state_variation, option_order_stability, cost_latency_summary, the sn-judge seat) carry no plan label, stage name, ticket number or version tag, and the changed prose is mechanism, not changelog.
rubric_items.reasoning: a finding — the §2 mechanism (delete the wrapper, route its callers through the shared owner, build any synchronous single-state entry point on decide_batch) loses the DecisionsValidationError contract that _call_judgment deliberately preserves, and decide_batch swallows every exception.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — §3 names one module plus the single-AUC-owner fold, and §2's two-part scope (owner consolidation, sn-judge seat) was already adjudicated and declined by an earlier review, with s2 changed since only in the mechanism paragraph, not its deliverables.
rubric_items.wiring: pass — §3 supplies the evaluation module that §4's three fixtures load "through §3", and the followup's partition of §2 (scope check), §3/§4 (disjoint paths) and §5 (coordinator labelling) names no missing external dependency for either changed unit; the block edges on the plan (sn-review-through-jev, sn-selection-over-generation, sn-catalog-grouping) are unchanged.
